title: Reverse Engineering 101
subtitle: Reading a compiled program you built, from file bytes to evidence-backed pseudocode, with rea and Ghidra
summary: How to read a compiled program without its source and prove what you found. Every listing comes from a recorded run of rea 6.7.0 and Ghidra 12.1.4 on programs written for this manual.
audience: You are an engineer who writes C, Python, or JavaScript and uses a coding agent. You have never read machine code with a decompiler. You want to understand what a compiled program does and to check what an agent tells you about it.
outcomes: Read the file header, sections, symbols, and relocations of a compiled program, and map an address to a file offset.
Run rea with the Ghidra provider on a program you built, and read its Evidence record: confidence, authority, limitations, and unknowns.
Find a function, read its assembly and pseudocode, follow its references, and say where the decompiler output is incomplete.
Prove a rebuilt function equal to the original by running both over an input grid and by comparing bytes after masking relocations.
Drive rea from an agent over MCP, and keep an evidence ledger that separates what was observed from what was inferred.

plate.title: One function, four views
plate.caption: The C you wrote, the six instructions clang made, the pseudocode Ghidra returned, and the Evidence record rea wrote for them, from capture/out/06-function-percent-change.json.

parts.title: rea on One Page
parts.thesis: rea asks an analysis engine about a program and returns each answer as an Evidence record that says how it knows.
parts.summary: What rea standardizes, what it leaves to Ghidra, and one complete investigation of a function.

parts.title: Authority and Setup
parts.thesis: You analyze a program only when you have the right to, and only after rea doctor reports the provider healthy.
parts.summary: The law and rea's responsible use rules, the Ghidra provider install, and the capabilities each command declares.

parts.title: The Artifact
parts.thesis: Before any engine runs, rea reads the file itself: its format, its load image, and where each address lives on disk.
parts.summary: inspect-artifact, the binary layout and Mach-O load image, address-to-file-offset, and the analyze overview.

parts.title: The Ghidra Provider
parts.thesis: Each question rea asks Ghidra becomes one bridge call into a fresh headless project, and the answer carries the limits of that engine.
parts.summary: open_binary and the bridge, procedures, assembly, references and the jump table, strings, and pseudocode.

parts.title: Evidence
parts.thesis: An Evidence record names its subject, its engine, its confidence, and its limits, and its id changes when any of them changes.
parts.summary: The Evidence record, residual unknowns, snapshots, bundles, and comparing two builds.

parts.title: Scripted and Managed Code
parts.thesis: For JavaScript, rea reads the files without running them and returns a graph of modules and their relationships.
parts.summary: analyze-javascript-application and the application graph, and inspect-wasm-artifact with the WABT provider.

parts.title: Rebuild and Prove
parts.thesis: rea records whether declared claims passed, so the proof that a rebuilt function is equal must come from your own tests.
parts.summary: verify_reconstruction and its limits, and a harness that proves a rebuild equal by execution and by bytes.

parts.title: Agents over MCP
parts.thesis: An agent reaches rea through one MCP server with 207 tools, and its findings are only as good as the evidence it keeps.
parts.summary: The MCP server, its tools and deadlines, and one agent investigation from question to evidence.
